All work is complete and verified. Here's my summary.

## Summary

I implemented issue #4262 — a `LoopGuard` vended plugin that detects a repeated tool batch, nudges, then ends the turn — built entirely on public hooks.

### What I changed
- **`strands-py/src/strands/vended_plugins/loop_guard/plugin.py`** — the `LoopGuard` plugin.
- **`strands-py/src/strands/vended_plugins/loop_guard/__init__.py`** — public export of `LoopGuard`.
- **`strands-py/tests/strands/vended_plugins/loop_guard/test_integration.py`** (+ `__init__.py`) — 7 end-to-end tests.

### Design decisions
- **Followed the existing vended-plugin patterns.** Like `GoalLoop`/`ContextInjector`, the plugin subclasses `Plugin`, exposes a `name` property (defaulting to `"strands:loop-guard"`, matching the `strands:*` convention), and registers hooks via the `@hook` decorator with event types inferred from type hints — no `init_agent` needed.
- **Two hooks, no event-loop changes.**
  - `BeforeToolsEvent`: computes an order-insensitive, id-agnostic signature of the batch (`sorted` list of per-call `json.dumps({"name", "input"}, sort_keys=True)`), skipping tools in `ignore`, and increments a per-signature count in `invocation_state`.
  - `AfterToolsEvent`: on reaching `nudge_after` repeats it appends a text block to `event.message["content"]` (the user-role tool-result message, so the note sits right under the results); on reaching `stop_after` it sets `event.end_turn` to the final text.
- **State lives only in `invocation_state`,** namespaced per plugin instance (`_loop_guard::<name>`), so it resets per invocation and survives interrupt/resume with no plugin-side memory.
- **Count-once-per-message-object:** a per-tool interrupt re-fires `BeforeToolsEvent` with the same assistant message object, so I dedupe by `id(event.message)` — a batch split across cycles counts once. `BeforeToolsEvent` communicates the current repeat count to `AfterToolsEvent` through a `pending` slot in the shared state, since the two events are paired within a cycle.
- **Provider neutral:** the guard never edits the assistant message, only the tool-result message and `end_turn`.
- **Configurable & validated:** `nudge_after=1`, `stop_after=2` (`None` = nudge only), `ignore`, and both texts with a `{tools}` placeholder (expands to sorted, comma-separated tool names). Constructor rejects `nudge_after < 1` and `stop_after < nudge_after`.

### How I verified it
- **7 unit tests, each driving a real `strands.Agent` through the event loop** with a scripted `MockedModelProvider` and real `@tool`s, covering exactly the suggested cases: note lands in the second tool-result turn; second repeat ends with `end_turn` and the model is called three times not four; a different batch is not a repeat; a shuffled batch is a repeat; `stop_after=None` nudges twice and lets the model finish; an ignored-only batch is never counted; and a batch split by a real per-tool interrupt (via `tool_context.interrupt` + resume) is counted once (no spurious nudge, with an assertion that `BeforeToolsEvent` actually fired ≥2 times).
- All 7 tests pass (`hatch run test`).
- `hatch run lint` passes; `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` are clean on the new files. (The two files `format-check` flagged for reformatting are pre-existing and untouched by me.)
- `git status` shows only the two new untracked directories; no commits or pushes made.

+"""LoopGuard plugin for Strands agents.
+
+Detects when the model asks for a tool batch it has already run — same tool
+names, same inputs — and first nudges, then ends the turn. Built entirely on
+public hooks (``BeforeToolsEvent`` and ``AfterToolsEvent``), so nothing inside
+the event loop changes.
+
+The batch signature is order-insensitive and ignores tool-use ids: two batches
+match when they request the same ``{name, input}`` set. Repeat counts live in
+``invocation_state``, so they reset per invocation and survive interrupt and
+resume without any plugin-side memory. The guard only ever edits the
+user-role tool-result message and ``AfterToolsEvent.end_turn`` — never the
+assistant message — so it is provider neutral.
+
+Example:
+    ```python
+    from strands import Agent
+    from strands.vended_plugins.loop_guard import LoopGuard
+
+    agent = Agent(tools=[...], plugins=[LoopGuard()])
+    ```
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import logging
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from typing import Any
+
+from ...hooks.events import AfterToolsEvent, BeforeToolsEvent
+from ...plugins import Plugin, hook
+from ...types.content import Message
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+_DEFAULT_NAME = "strands:loop-guard"
+"""Default plugin name; override to tell multiple guards apart."""
+
+_DEFAULT_NUDGE = (
+    "Note: this exact tool batch ({tools}) was already run this turn and its results are above. "
+    "Reuse those results instead of requesting the same calls again."
+)
+"""Default nudge text, appended under the tool results the model already has."""
+
+_DEFAULT_STOP = (
+    "Ending the turn: the tool batch ({tools}) was requested repeatedly with identical inputs and "
+    "the results are already in the conversation."
+)
+"""Default final text used when the repeat crosses ``stop_after``."""
+
+
+class LoopGuard(Plugin):
+    """Plugin that detects a repeated tool batch, nudges, then ends the turn.
+
+    A repeated batch is one whose ``toolUse`` blocks request the same
+    ``{name, input}`` set as a batch already run this invocation. Ordering and
+    tool-use ids do not matter; a shuffled batch is still a repeat.
+
+    On each tool batch the guard computes a signature from the assistant
+    message and counts it in ``invocation_state``. When the number of *repeats*
+    (occurrences after the first) reaches ``nudge_after``, it appends a short
+    text block to the tool-result message so the model reads the note directly
+    under the results it already has. When repeats reach ``stop_after``, it sets
+    ``AfterToolsEvent.end_turn`` so the run stops with ``stop_reason ==
+    "end_turn"`` instead of burning the remaining budget.
+
+    State lives entirely in ``invocation_state``: it resets per invocation and
+    survives interrupt and resume. A per-tool interrupt re-fires
+    ``BeforeToolsEvent`` with the same assistant message; the guard counts that
+    message object once by identity, so a batch split across cycles counts as a
+    single occurrence.
+
+    Args:
+        nudge_after: Number of repeats (occurrences after the first) at or above
+            which the guard appends the nudge. Defaults to ``1`` (the first
+            repeat). Must be at least ``1``.
+        stop_after: Number of repeats at or above which the guard ends the turn,
+            or ``None`` to nudge only and never stop. Defaults to ``2``. When
+            set, must be at least ``nudge_after``.
+        ignore: Tool names to exclude from the signature — non-idempotent tools
+            (live readings, clocks) whose repeat is not a wasted cycle. A batch
+            made up entirely of ignored tools is never counted.
+        nudge_text: Nudge text. Supports a ``{tools}`` placeholder that expands
+            to the sorted, comma-separated tool names in the batch.
+        stop_text: Final text used when a repeat crosses ``stop_after``. Supports
+            the same ``{tools}`` placeholder.
+        name: Plugin name, for logging and duplicate detection. Defaults to
+            ``"strands:loop-guard"``. Set a distinct name when registering more
+            than one guard.
+
+    Example:
+        ```python
+        from strands import Agent
+        from strands.vended_plugins.loop_guard import LoopGuard
+
+        agent = Agent(
+            tools=[...],
+            plugins=[LoopGuard(nudge_after=1, stop_after=2, ignore=["get_clock"])],
+        )
+        ```
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        nudge_after: int = 1,
+        stop_after: int | None = 2,
+        ignore: Iterable[str] | None = None,
+        nudge_text: str = _DEFAULT_NUDGE,
+        stop_text: str = _DEFAULT_STOP,
+        name: str | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Initialize the LoopGuard plugin.
+
+        Args:
+            nudge_after: Repeats at or above which to nudge. Defaults to ``1``.
+            stop_after: Repeats at or above which to end the turn, or ``None``
+                to nudge only. Defaults to ``2``.
+            ignore: Tool names to exclude from the signature.
+            nudge_text: Nudge text with an optional ``{tools}`` placeholder.
+            stop_text: Final text with an optional ``{tools}`` placeholder.
+            name: Plugin name. Defaults to ``"strands:loop-guard"``.
+
+        Raises:
+            ValueError: If ``nudge_after < 1`` or ``stop_after < nudge_after``.
+        """
+        if nudge_after < 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"nudge_after=<{nudge_after}> | must be at least 1")
+        if stop_after is not None and stop_after < nudge_after:
+            raise ValueError(f"stop_after=<{stop_after}> | must be >= nudge_after=<{nudge_after}>")
+
+        self._name = name or _DEFAULT_NAME
+        self._nudge_after = nudge_after
+        self._stop_after = stop_after
+        self._ignore = frozenset(ignore or ())
+        self._nudge_text = nudge_text
+        self._stop_text = stop_text
+        # A distinct namespace per plugin instance so multiple guards on one
+        # agent keep separate counts within the same invocation_state.
+        self._state_key = f"_loop_guard::{self._name}"
+        super().__init__()
+
+    @property
+    def name(self) -> str:
+        """Plugin name."""
+        return self._name
+
+    @hook
+    def _count_batch(self, event: BeforeToolsEvent) -> None:
+        """Count the batch signature once per assistant message in ``invocation_state``."""
+        signature, _ = self._signature(event.message)
+        if signature is None:
+            return
+
+        state = self._state(event.invocation_state)
+        counted: set[int] = state["counted_message_ids"]
+        counts: dict[str, int] = state["counts"]
+
+        # A per-tool interrupt re-fires this event with the same assistant
+        # message object; count that batch once by identity.
+        message_id = id(event.message)
+        if message_id not in counted:
+            counted.add(message_id)
+            counts[signature] = counts.get(signature, 0) + 1
+
+        # Repeats = occurrences after the first. Hand it to AfterToolsEvent,
+        # which owns the tool-result message and end_turn.
+        state["pending"] = {"repeats": counts[signature] - 1, "signature": signature}
+
+    @hook
+    def _act_on_repeat(self, event: AfterToolsEvent) -> None:
+        """Nudge on a repeat, then end the turn once ``stop_after`` is crossed."""
+        state = self._state(event.invocation_state)
+        pending = state.get("pending")
+        if not pending:
+            return
+
+        repeats: int = pending["repeats"]
+        if repeats < self._nudge_after:
+            return
+
+        tools = self._tools_label(pending["signature"])
+
+        if self._stop_after is not None and repeats >= self._stop_after:
+            event.end_turn = self._stop_text.format(tools=tools)
+            logger.debug("loop_guard=<%s> | repeats=<%d> | ending turn", self._name, repeats)
+            return
+
+        event.message["content"].append({"text": self._nudge_text.format(tools=tools)})
+        logger.debug("loop_guard=<%s> | repeats=<%d> | nudging", self._name, repeats)
+
+    def _state(self, invocation_state: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        """Return this guard's mutable state within ``invocation_state``, creating it once."""
+        state = invocation_state.get(self._state_key)
+        if state is None:
+            state = {"counts": {}, "counted_message_ids": set(), "pending": None}
+            invocation_state[self._state_key] = state
+        return state
+
+    def _signature(self, message: Message) -> tuple[str | None, list[str]]:
+        """Compute an order-insensitive, id-agnostic signature of a tool batch.
+
+        Returns ``(signature, tool_names)`` where ``signature`` is ``None`` when
+        the batch has no countable (non-ignored) tool uses.
+        """
+        parts: list[str] = []
+        tool_names: list[str] = []
+        for block in message.get("content", []):
+            tool_use = block.get("toolUse")
+            if not tool_use:
+                continue
+            name = tool_use.get("name")
+            if name in self._ignore:
+                continue
+            tool_names.append(name)
+            # sort_keys makes the per-call JSON canonical; sorting the list of
+            # per-call strings below makes the batch order-insensitive.
+            parts.append(json.dumps({"name": name, "input": tool_use.get("input")}, sort_keys=True))
+
+        if not parts:
+            return None, []
+
+        return json.dumps(sorted(parts)), tool_names
+
+    def _tools_label(self, signature: str) -> str:
+        """Render the ``{tools}`` placeholder: sorted, unique, comma-separated names."""
+        names = sorted({json.loads(part)["name"] for part in json.loads(signature)})
+        return ", ".join(names)

+"""End-to-end tests for LoopGuard against a real Agent + event loop.
+
+Each test drives a real ``strands.Agent`` through the event loop with a scripted
+``MockedModelProvider`` and a real ``@tool``. They verify the two behaviors the
+guard promises — a nudge on the first repeat and an ``end_turn`` on the second —
+plus the signature semantics (order-insensitive, id-agnostic) and the
+count-once-per-message-object contract under a per-tool interrupt.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+
+from strands import Agent, tool
+from strands.hooks import BeforeToolsEvent
+from strands.types.content import Message
+from strands.types.tools import ToolContext
+from strands.vended_plugins.loop_guard import LoopGuard
+from tests.fixtures.mocked_model_provider import MockedModelProvider
+
+
+@tool
+def read_data(pid: str) -> str:
+    """Read a (fake) idempotent data series for a pid."""
+    return f"series:{pid}"
+
+
+@tool
+def read_other(pid: str) -> str:
+    """Read a second (fake) idempotent data series for a pid."""
+    return f"other:{pid}"
+
+
+def _tool_use(name: str, tool_use_id: str, **inputs) -> dict:
+    return {"toolUse": {"name": name, "toolUseId": tool_use_id, "input": inputs}}
+
+
+def _assistant(*blocks: dict) -> Message:
+    return {"role": "assistant", "content": list(blocks)}
+
+
+def _tool_result_messages(agent: Agent) -> list[Message]:
+    """User-role messages that carry tool results, in order."""
+    return [
+        message
+        for message in agent.messages
+        if message["role"] == "user" and any("toolResult" in block for block in message["content"])
+    ]
+
+
+def _texts_of(message: Message) -> list[str]:
+    return [block["text"] for block in message["content"] if "text" in block]
+
+
+def _all_text(agent: Agent) -> str:
+    return " ".join(text for message in agent.messages for text in _texts_of(message))
+
+
+def test_nudge_lands_in_the_second_tool_result_turn():
+    """On the first repeat, the note is a text block on the second tool-result message."""
+    batch = _tool_use("read_data", "t1", pid="A")
+    model = MockedModelProvider(
+        [
+            _assistant(batch),  # occurrence 1 — no action
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t2", pid="A")),  # repeat 1 — nudge
+            {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "done"}]},
+        ]
+    )
+    agent = Agent(model=model, tools=[read_data], plugins=[LoopGuard()], callback_handler=None)
+
+    agent("look at pid A")
+
+    tool_results = _tool_result_messages(agent)
+    assert len(tool_results) == 2
+    # First tool-result turn carries only results, no note.
+    assert _texts_of(tool_results[0]) == []
+    # Second tool-result turn carries the nudge, and it names the tool.
+    assert len(_texts_of(tool_results[1])) == 1
+    assert "read_data" in _texts_of(tool_results[1])[0]
+
+
+def test_second_repeat_ends_turn_and_calls_model_three_times():
+    """The second repeat halts the run with end_turn; the model is called three times, not four."""
+    model = MockedModelProvider(
+        [
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t1", pid="A")),  # occurrence 1
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t2", pid="A")),  # repeat 1 — nudge
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t3", pid="A")),  # repeat 2 — end_turn
+            # A fourth response exists but must never be consumed.
+            {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "should not be reached"}]},
+        ]
+    )
+    agent = Agent(model=model, tools=[read_data], plugins=[LoopGuard()], callback_handler=None)
+
+    result = agent("look at pid A")
+
+    assert result.stop_reason == "end_turn"
+    assert model.index == 3  # called three times, not four
+    assert "should not be reached" not in _all_text(agent)
+    # The final assistant message is the guard's stop text.
+    assert "read_data" in _texts_of(agent.messages[-1])[0]
+
+
+def test_different_batch_is_not_a_repeat():
+    """A different batch (different inputs) never triggers a nudge or an end_turn."""
+    model = MockedModelProvider(
+        [
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t1", pid="A")),
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t2", pid="B")),  # different input
+            {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "done"}]},
+        ]
+    )
+    agent = Agent(model=model, tools=[read_data], plugins=[LoopGuard()], callback_handler=None)
+
+    result = agent("look at A then B")
+
+    assert result.stop_reason == "end_turn"
+    assert model.index == 3
+    # No nudge was appended to either tool-result turn.
+    assert all(_texts_of(message) == [] for message in _tool_result_messages(agent))
+
+
+def test_shuffled_batch_is_a_repeat():
+    """The same batch with its calls reordered is still a repeat, so it nudges."""
+    first = _assistant(
+        _tool_use("read_data", "t1", pid="A"),
+        _tool_use("read_other", "t2", pid="A"),
+    )
+    shuffled = _assistant(
+        _tool_use("read_other", "t3", pid="A"),  # reversed order, new ids
+        _tool_use("read_data", "t4", pid="A"),
+    )
+    model = MockedModelProvider([first, shuffled, {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "done"}]}])
+    agent = Agent(model=model, tools=[read_data, read_other], plugins=[LoopGuard()], callback_handler=None)
+
+    agent("look at pid A")
+
+    tool_results = _tool_result_messages(agent)
+    notes = _texts_of(tool_results[1])
+    assert len(notes) == 1
+    assert "read_data" in notes[0] and "read_other" in notes[0]
+
+
+def test_stop_after_none_nudges_and_lets_the_model_finish():
+    """With stop_after=None the guard only nudges; the run finishes on the model's own turn."""
+    model = MockedModelProvider(
+        [
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t1", pid="A")),  # occurrence 1
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t2", pid="A")),  # repeat 1 — nudge
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t3", pid="A")),  # repeat 2 — nudge (no stop)
+            {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "final answer"}]},
+        ]
+    )
+    agent = Agent(
+        model=model,
+        tools=[read_data],
+        plugins=[LoopGuard(stop_after=None)],
+        callback_handler=None,
+    )
+
+    result = agent("look at pid A")
+
+    assert result.stop_reason == "end_turn"
+    assert model.index == 4  # the model, not the guard, ended the run
+    assert "final answer" in _all_text(agent)
+    # Two nudges landed — one per repeat.
+    nudged = [message for message in _tool_result_messages(agent) if _texts_of(message)]
+    assert len(nudged) == 2
+
+
+def test_ignored_tool_batch_is_never_counted():
+    """A batch made only of ignored tools is not a repeat, so it never nudges."""
+    model = MockedModelProvider(
+        [
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t1", pid="A")),
+            _assistant(_tool_use("read_data", "t2", pid="A")),  # would be a repeat, but ignored
+            {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "done"}]},
+        ]
+    )
+    agent = Agent(
+        model=model,
+        tools=[read_data],
+        plugins=[LoopGuard(ignore=["read_data"])],
+        callback_handler=None,
+    )
+
+    agent("look at pid A")
+
+    assert all(_texts_of(message) == [] for message in _tool_result_messages(agent))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_batch_split_by_interrupt_is_counted_once():
+    """A per-tool interrupt re-fires BeforeToolsEvent on the same message; it counts once (no nudge)."""
+
+    @tool(context=True)
+    def confirm(tool_context: ToolContext) -> str:
+        """Require confirmation before completing."""
+        response = tool_context.interrupt("confirm", reason="Confirm?")
+        return f"confirmed:{response}"
+
+    model = MockedModelProvider(
+        [
+            _assistant(
+                _tool_use("read_data", "t1", pid="A"),
+                {"toolUse": {"name": "confirm", "toolUseId": "t2", "input": {}}},
+            ),
+            {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "done"}]},
+        ]
+    )
+    agent = Agent(model=model, tools=[read_data, confirm], plugins=[LoopGuard()], callback_handler=None)
+
+    # Confirm the batch is genuinely split: BeforeToolsEvent fires more than once.
+    before_tools_fires = 0
+
+    def _count(event: BeforeToolsEvent) -> None:
+        nonlocal before_tools_fires
+        before_tools_fires += 1
+
+    agent.hooks.add_callback(BeforeToolsEvent, _count)
+
+    interrupted = await agent.invoke_async("look at pid A")
+    assert interrupted.stop_reason == "interrupt"
+
+    final = await agent.invoke_async(
+        [{"interruptResponse": {"interruptId": interrupted.interrupts[0].id, "response": "yes"}}]
+    )
+
+    assert final.stop_reason == "end_turn"
+    assert before_tools_fires >= 2  # the batch really was split across cycles
+    # Counted once, so it is not a repeat: no nudge anywhere.
+    assert all(_texts_of(message) == [] for message in _tool_result_messages(agent))
